theme: Complete candidate identity and participant exposure review
question: Can all 358 candidate inventory rows receive source-attributed identity and exposure dispositions using held metadata without a new primary-content read?
outcome: Reviewed all 358 rows. Verified 24 existing provisional-family identifier links; retained 306 candidate-only rows and 28 unlinked rows. Indexed 1018 historical exposure records and 2139 candidate-event associations. Preserved 11 unresolved duplicate flags and two shared-registration pairs. Distinguished 313 explicit PDF-page matches from 45 derived-page matches with unverified original PDF binding. No physical merges or confirmation-eligible rows.
challenge: Inventory rows are not unique physical objects. Site and project labels complicate complete-identifier matching. Exposure logs mix script access, model display, conservative incident sets and derived page coordinates.
remedy: Used narrow site-qualified namespace rules, preserved all numeric components and unresolved relations, separated access and display classes, retained participant and page uncertainty, and verified deterministic local exports. Logged incidental source-derived metadata displayed during workflow inspection.
retry_when: New object-specific identity evidence, original-PDF page bindings, exact historical display records or a declared future participant and statistic-family policy becomes available.

authors.model: GPT-6 family; exact backend identifier not exposed
